# Hewatell — Air Quality Monitor

The Hewatell Air Quality Monitor is a professional, mobile Internet of Things (IoT) environment surveillance dashboard designed to track localized air conditions in real-time. Built using the Flutter framework and a cloud-native Firebase backend, the application translates complex atmospheric data into intuitive, visual metrics that help users monitor and protect their health.

## Core Tracking Parameters and Scientific Scales

The application actively monitors five distinct environmental gas profiles, each calibrated within specific safety boundaries to ensure accurate health metrics:

- **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂):** Monitored from 400 to 1,500 ppm. High levels indicate poor ventilation, leading to drowsiness or headaches.
- **Nitrogen (N₂):** Tracked from 0 to 500 ppm to monitor general gaseous composition changes in the immediate atmosphere.
- **Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC):** Tracked from 0.00 to 3.00 ppm to catch chemical fumes, smoke, or toxic household vapors.
- **Dust / Particulate Matter (PM10):** Monitored from 0 to 100 micrograms per cubic meter to measure fine dust or smoke pollution levels.
- **Ethylene Gas (C₂H₄):** Scaled from 0.000 to 0.200 ppm, primarily used for sensitive agricultural or storage decay tracing.

## Key System Features and Screen Layouts

The application architecture shifts views away from the main setup files into dedicated, clean screen modules.

### 1. Authentication Gate

A unified, clean Teal-themed layout managing Sign In and Sign Up inputs on a single page, alongside a high-security Google verification sign-in channel.

### 2. Main Workspace Dashboard

The control panel hub that routes verified users seamlessly into sub-system modules, including a logout trigger that safely clears device sessions.

<img src="data:image/png;base64," width="320" alt="Dashboard screen with Register New Device, Select Existing Device, View Current Data, and View Previous Data options">

### 3. Register New Hardware

A minimalist form with clean, underlined text inputs for Device Name, Device ID, and Location, linking physical monitor serial keys directly to Cloud Firestore.

<img src="data:image/png;base64," width="320" alt="Register New Device screen with Device Name, Device ID, and Location fields">

### 4. Select Paired Monitor

A real-time database-fetching list that lets users filter and pick specific registered hardware monitors using an interactive search bar with custom text.

<img src="data:image/png;base64," width="320" alt="Select Existing Device screen showing a registered device">

### 5. Real-Time Data Gauges

The core mission control panel featuring a large, animated speedometer dial for Carbon Dioxide, alongside a two-column grid layout housing smaller radial dials for the other four gases. It updates dynamically every 3 seconds and randomizes local neighborhoods to simulate a mobile tracking station.

<img src="data:image/png;base64," width="320" alt="Current Sensor Data screen with a CO2 gauge and a 2x2 grid of gas gauges">

### 6. Historical Analytics Chart

A comprehensive analytics dashboard utilizing a native calendar date range picker. Once a user clicks the "Request Data" button, a shared data repository pipeline pulls stored entries and maps them onto a professional, fluid line graph over an explicit grid layout.

<img src="data:image/png;base64," width="320" alt="Date range picker for selecting a historical data window">

Users can switch between parameters to plot — CO₂, Nitrogen, VOC, Dust, and Ethylene — each rendered as its own trend chart with a log of captured readings below it.

## Technical Stack Architecture

The entire project operates on a modern, decoupled development architecture:

- **Frontend UI Engine:** Flutter SDK utilizing Material 3 design parameters.
- **Visual Graph Compilers:** Syncfusion Flutter Gauges and FL Chart data packages.
- **Cloud Infrastructure:** Firebase Authentication for user token security and Cloud Firestore for the NoSQL live streaming database.
- **Synchronization Pipeline:** A centralized, shared runtime repository holding sensor logs in phone memory during local loop simulations.

## Local Deployment Guide

To deploy or review this workspace configuration on your computer, ensure your setup meets these benchmarks:

- **Operating System:** Ubuntu Linux with the Flutter mobile SDK and Android Studio properly installed.
- **Dependency Installation:** Navigate to the project root directory in your local terminal and run the `flutter pub get` command to fetch code libraries.
- **Handset Compilation:** Plug in your physical handset (such as your connected Infinix phone), verify connection visibility with `flutter devices`, and compile the application binaries straight onto your device screen by executing the `flutter run` command.
